## HIGH IMPACT

No clearly confirmed HIGH severity breaking changes can be derived from the single changed file in this diff (`src/components/ha-entity-type-picker.ts`, which appears to be empty/binary). However, several changes in the release notes describe structural removals that are HIGH severity for ha-lcars and are confirmed by the PR descriptions below.

### Component: `ha-outlined-icon-button` → `ha-icon-button` (Migration)

**What changed:** PR #54571 "Migrate ha-outlined-icon-button to ha-icon-button" removes `ha-outlined-icon-button` as a distinct element. Any card-mod CSS selector targeting `ha-outlined-icon-button` in the shadow DOM will silently stop matching.

**LCARS rules affected:** The preamble does not currently appear to directly target `ha-outlined-icon-button` by name, but if any downstream custom card or UIX injection in the theme uses it, those selectors will be dead.

**Suggested fix:** Search all theme source files for `ha-outlined-icon-button` and replace with `ha-icon-button`. No fix needed if not present.

---

### Component: `ha-md-list` / `ha-md-list-item` — Removed

**What changed:** PR #54569 "Migrate remaining ha-md-list usages and remove ha-md-list" removes the `ha-md-list` and `ha-md-list-item` custom elements entirely from the HA frontend.

**LCARS rules affected:** The `card-mod-config-yaml` block in `preamble.yaml` directly targets these elements:

```yaml
"ha-config-info $ hass-subpage div.content":
  "ha-card": |
    :is(.pages) {
      ha-md-list {
        --md-sys-color-surface: transparent !important;
        ha-md-list-item { ... }
        ha-md-list-item:first-child { ... }
        ha-md-list-item:last-child { ... }
      }
    }
```

With `ha-md-list` and `ha-md-list-item` removed, these selectors will never match. The info page list items will lose their LCARS color styling (top/mid/bottom bar colors, border-radius 999px pills).

**Suggested fix:** Determine the replacement element names. Based on the migration pattern in this release (see also `ha-list-nav` / `ha-list-item-button` usage elsewhere in the theme), the new elements are likely `ha-list-nav` and `ha-list-item-button`. Update the `ha-config-info` card-mod block to:

```yaml
"ha-config-info $ hass-subpage div.content":
  "ha-card": |
    :is(.pages) {
      ha-list-nav {
        --md-sys-color-surface: transparent !important;
        padding-top: 0px;
        ha-list-item-button { ... }
        ha-list-item-button:first-child { ... }
        ha-list-item-button:last-child { ... }
      }
    }
```

---

### Component: `--mdc-typography-*` CSS Custom Properties — Removed

**What changed:** PR #54201 "Remove dead --mdc-typography-* custom properties" removes the `--mdc-typography-*` family of CSS custom properties from the HA frontend entirely.

**LCARS rules affected:** The `&base` block in `preamble.yaml` defines and relies on:

```yaml
mdc-typography-button-font-family: var(--font-family)
mdc-typography-body2-font-family: var(--font-family)
mdc-typography-font-family: var(--font-family)
```

These variables (rendered as `--mdc-typography-button-font-family`, `--mdc-typography-body2-font-family`, `--mdc-typography-font-family`) are now dead — HA no longer reads them. The Tungsten/Antonio font will not be applied via these tokens to any MDC-controlled text that previously consumed them.

**Suggested fix:** Remove these three entries from the `&base` block. Font application to MDC-derived components must now rely on `--font-family` / `ha-font-family-body` (already defined in `&base`) or direct `font-family` overrides in card-mod CSS selectors. Audit which UI elements visually lost the LCARS font and add targeted `font-family: var(--font-family)` rules in the appropriate `card-mod-config-yaml` or `card-mod-dialog-yaml` blocks.

---

### Component: `@material/web` — Package Removed

**What changed:** PR #54580 "Remove @material/web" removes the entire `@material/web` package from the HA frontend. All `--md-*` custom properties that were consumed by Material Web components are gone.

**LCARS rules affected:** The `&base` block and `card-mod-config-yaml` blocks define and rely on:

```yaml
mdc-shape-small: 0px                    # --mdc-shape-small
--md-sys-color-primary: var(--lcars-ui-quaternary)  # in card-mod-card-yaml
--md-sys-color-surface: ...              # in card-mod-config-yaml, card-mod-dialog-yaml, card-mod-more-info-yaml, ha-config-info pages block, ha-config-section-updates block, ha-config-repairs-dashboard block
```

Specifically, these injections will now be no-ops:

- `--md-sys-color-primary: var(--lcars-ui-quaternary) !important` (in `card-mod-card-yaml` `:host` block)
- `--md-sys-color-surface: var(--lcars-settings-card-color)` (in `card-mod-config-yaml`, `card-mod-dialog-yaml`, `card-mod-more-info-yaml`)
- `--md-sys-color-surface: transparent !important` (in repairs, updates, and info page sub-blocks)
- `mdc-shape-small: 0px` in `&base`

Cards and dialogs that relied on `--md-sys-color-surface` for their background color may revert to HA defaults, breaking the LCARS medium-gray settings card background.

**Suggested fix:**
1. Remove `mdc-shape-small: 0px` from `&base`.
2. Identify the replacement surface/background token. In the new HA design system (WebAwesome-based), the equivalent is likely `--ha-card-background` or `--card-background-color` (already set in `&base`) or a new `--wa-*` token. Verify which token the settings panels, dialogs, and more-info overlays now use for their background, then update `card-mod-config-yaml`, `card-mod-dialog-yaml`, and `card-mod-more-info-yaml` accordingly.
3. The `--md-sys-color-primary` injection in `card-mod-card-yaml` should be replaced with whatever the new primary color token is for the WebAwesome component system (check for `--wa-color-fill-normal` or similar).

---

### Component: `ha-formfield` — Removed

**What changed:** PR #54200 "Drop ha-formfield in favour of the switch's own label" removes the `ha-formfield` wrapper element.

**LCARS rules affected:** No direct `ha-formfield` selectors appear in the ha-lcars preamble source shown. However, if any sub-selectors in the config or dialog card-mod blocks relied on `ha-formfield` as part of a compound selector chain to reach `ha-switch` or label elements, those chains are now broken.

**Suggested fix:** Search all theme source for `ha-formfield`. If found, replace with the switch element's own label structure. If not found, no fix needed.

---

## MEDIUM IMPACT

### Component: `ha-list` — Removed from Gallery / Reduced Usage

**What changed:** PR #55393 "Remove unused ha-list imports and migrate gallery off ha-list" reduces `ha-list` usage. This is separate from `ha-md-list` removal. The `ha-list` element itself appears to still exist but has reduced scope.

**LCARS rules affected:** The `card-mod-card-yaml` todo-list block targets:

```css
ha-sortable > ha-list {
  .header { ... }
  ha-check-list-item { ... }
}
```

And the `card-mod-row-yaml` sub-selector:

```yaml
"ha-card ha-sortable ha-list":
  "ha-check-list-item$": |
```

If the todo-list card's internal structure no longer uses `ha-list` as the wrapping element for sortable items, these selectors will stop matching.

**Suggested fix:** Test the to-do list card after update. If the `ha-sortable > ha-list` selector stops working, inspect the new shadow DOM structure and update the selector to match whatever element replaced `ha-list` in the todo card's internal template.

---

### Component: Avatar/Entity Picture Border Radius Change

**What changed:** PR #54902 "Use rounded squares for avatars and entity pictures" changes avatar and entity picture display from circles to rounded squares.

**LCARS rules affected:** The LCARS sidebar targets `ha-user-badge`:

```css
ha-user-badge {
  box-sizing: border-box;
  width: calc(var(--mdc-icon-size,24px) + 37px);
  padding-block: 8px;
}
```

The user badge (avatar) in the sidebar will now display as a rounded square instead of a circle. This is not necessarily wrong for LCARS aesthetics but represents a visible change.

**Suggested fix:** If the rounded square style is acceptable for LCARS, no change needed. If circle avatars are desired, add `border-radius: 50%` to the `ha-user-badge` rule in `card-mod-sidebar-yaml`.

---

### Component: `ha-ripple` — Custom Implementation Replacing Material Base

**What changed:** PR #54508 "Replace ha-ripple Material base with own implementation" replaces the Material ripple with a custom HA implementation.

**LCARS rules affected:** The `card-mod-card-yaml` button section sets:

```css
--ha-ripple-color: var(--lcars-ripple-color);
--ha-ripple-pressed-opacity: var(--lcars-ripple-pressed-opacity);
--ha-ripple-hover-opacity: var(--lcars-ripple-hover-opacity);
```

These variable names (`--ha-ripple-color`, `--ha-ripple-pressed-opacity`, `--ha-ripple-hover-opacity`) should continue to work if the new custom implementation preserved the same CSS custom property API. However, if the new implementation changed the property names, the louder ripple feedback on LCARS buttons will silently revert to HA defaults.

**Suggested fix:** Verify that `--ha-ripple-color`, `--ha-ripple-pressed-opacity`, and `--ha-ripple-hover-opacity` are still the correct property names in the new custom ripple implementation. If renamed, update `defaults.yaml` (`lcars-ripple-color`, `lcars-ripple-pressed-opacity`, `lcars-ripple-hover-opacity`) and the card-mod button block accordingly.

---

### Component: Gauge Card — Fit to Card Height in Sections View

**What changed:** PR #55260 "Fit gauge card to the card height in sections view" changes how gauge cards size themselves.

**LCARS rules affected:** The `card-mod-card-yaml` contains:

```yaml
"ha-card ha-gauge$": |
  .gauge {
    --primary-background-color: var(--lcars-dark-gray);
  }
```

The internal sizing change may affect how the `.gauge` element is laid out, potentially causing overflow or unexpected display with the LCARS `height: 100%` card model.

**Suggested fix:** Test gauge cards in sections view. If the gauge overflows or misaligns with the LCARS card frame, add explicit `height` constraints to the `ha-card ha-gauge$` card-mod block.

---

### Component: Sections View — New Section Types and Backgrounds

**What changed:** Multiple PRs (#55150, #54930, #54624, #55190) add new section type dialogs, section backgrounds visible in the sidebar, entity section strategies, and device section strategies.

**LCARS rules affected:** The `card-mod-root-yaml` `#view` block styles the lovelace view:

```css
#view {
  --lovelace-background: var(--primary-background-color);
  ...
}
```

New section background options rendered by HA may not inherit or respect the LCARS background color variable chain, causing sections with custom backgrounds to visually clash with the LCARS theme.

**Suggested fix:** Test section backgrounds in the sections dashboard view. If HA renders section backgrounds using a new CSS variable (e.g., `--section-background-color`), add it to the `#view` block or the `card-mod-card-yaml` `:host` block as appropriate.

---

### Component: `--mdc-select-*` and `--mdc-text-field-*` Variables

**What changed:** The removal of `@material/web` (PR #54580) and `--mdc-typography-*` variables (PR #54201) is part of a broader MDC teardown. The remaining `--mdc-*` variables in the `&base` block may also be progressively abandoned.

**LCARS rules affected:** The `&base` block defines:

```yaml
mdc-select-label-ink-color: var(--lcars-secondary-text)
mdc-select-ink-color: var(--lcars-primary-text)
mdc-text-field-label-ink-color: var(--lcars-primary-text)
```

With the MDC teardown ongoing, select and text-field components that previously used these tokens may have migrated to WebAwesome equivalents (`--wa-*`). Text fields and select dropdowns in dialogs and config panels may show incorrect text/fill colors.

**Suggested fix:** Audit the HA frontend source for what CSS custom properties `ha-textfield`, `ha-select`, and related components now consume. Replace dead `--mdc-*` tokens in `&base` with their WebAwesome or HA-native equivalents. The `wa-form-control-value-color: var(--lcars-primary-text)` entry already in `&base` suggests this migration is partially underway — extend it.
